title: Locked-model handshake and prompt stability specification
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define a prescriptive compatibility 'handshake' that locked/pinned model versions must satisfy before being published to customers. The spec covers prompt and input schema stability, parameter tolerances, structured-output guarantees, and a published performance profile (latency/throughput/memory). The goal is to allow teams to pin a model version with clear expectations about behavior and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable handshake manifest format is drafted and reviewed (fields listed below)
CI job that validates model artifacts against the handshake manifest for new pinned versions exists and passes on sample prompt suites
Rollout gates defined: canary policy, regression thresholds, rollback triggers, and observability dashboard widgets
Performance profile publishing pipeline emits P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory footprint and kv-cache footprints for the pinned variant
Developer-facing docs and sample prompts showing permitted prompt evolutions and deprecated constructs are published
handshake_manifest_fields: structured_output_schema (JSON schema or protobuf) when applicable
kv_cache_compatibility_flag (requires KV cache migration note when true)
fallback_compatible_variants (list of model_version keys to route to if primary unavailable)
compatibility_signature_hash (artifact checksum to detect silent rebuilds)
validation_steps: Run regression prompts (customer and internal representative set) against new pinned artifact
Schema validation of structured outputs using JSON schemas tied to the handshake
Parameter sweep: run sample requests across boundary parameter values to detect non-linear behavior
Performance profiling on representative hardware shapes (hosted small, dedicated gpus, private on-prem config)
Check tokenizer invariants (token counts for canonical prompts) and ensure no tokenization drift
Run compatibility linter against client SDKs to detect breaking param name/enum changes
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Strict guarantees vs. flexible tolerances: prefer explicit tolerance ranges rather than absolute immutability for numeric params to reduce churn on micro-adjustments
Freeze structured-output schemas for pinned versions; minor whitespace/ordering differences acceptable but schema must validate
Publish both logical API promises (schema, param names) and empirical performance profiles; accept that performance profiles are environment-dependent and include hardware labels
Allow model implementers to add compatible internal optimizations (kernel swaps, fused ops) provided the compatibility signature hash is updated and regression harness passes
review_comments: PM review (June): Clarify customer communication for deprecated prompt constructs — ACTION: add migration examples
Design review: Add explicit examples for chat vs. single-turn prompt shape mapping
Security review (Ruth): Ensure handshake manifest does not leak internal paths or secrets
Ops review: Require performance profile to include memory high-water mark and kv-cache delta on warm/hot starts
open_tasks: Draft handshake manifest JSON schema in repository: models/handshake/handshake-v1.schema.json
Add CI pipeline step: handshake-validate that loads manifest and runs regression suite
Instrument runtime to emit handshake_compliance metric for pinned-serving paths
Add UI in Console to display handshake fields on pinned model pages and expose download for customers
Create migration guide for customers when a pinned model is replaced by a compatible variant
notes: We discovered an incident where tokenizer changes in a downstream fork caused token-count drift; handshake schema must require tokenizer_version to pin tokenization semantics
Quantized build variations should be labeled separately but can be declared compatible if output schema and decoding are identical
For private/VPC installs, include an extra field in the handshake manifest declaring any required infra knobs (e.g., pin CUDA/cuDNN versions)
final_comment: This ticket codifies the onboarding checklist and CI gating for a first-class pinned model handshake. Implementation will be iterative; first cut focuses on schema, CI validation, and perf profile publishing. Follow-on tickets will add Console UI and extended migration tooling.
